messages.content: How far will a car travel in time 't' when launched with velocity 'v' at an angle 'theta'?

function.name: calculate_projectile_range
function.description: Calculate the range of a projectile launched at an angle with initial velocity, using the kinematic equation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

initial_velocity.description: The initial velocity at which projectile is launched. This is a float type value.

angle.description: The angle at which projectile is launched. This should be in degrees. This is a float type value.

time.description: The time in seconds after which the range is to be calculated. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The horizontal distance (range) a projectile travels after a time \(t\) when launched with speed \(v\) at an angle \(\theta\) (measured from the horizontal) is simply

\[
\text{range}(t)=v\,\cos(\theta)\;t .
\]

So, for example, if a car is launched at \(v=20\;\text{m/s}\) and \(\theta=30^\circ\), then after \(t=5\;\text{s}\) it would have covered

\[
20\;\text{m/s}\times\cos(30^\circ)\times5\;\text{s}\approx 86.6\;\text{m}.
\]

---

### Using the provided function

If you want to let the `calculate_projectile_range` function do the calculation, you need to supply numeric values for `initial_velocity`, `angle`, and optionally `time`. For instance:

```python
result = calculate_projectile_range(
    initial_velocity=20,   # m/s
    angle=30,              # degrees
    time=5                 # seconds
)
```

The function will return the same value as the formula above. If you only provide `initial_velocity` and `angle`, it will default to `time=0.5 s`.
